strings.2 stations will be adjusted according to: 2 stations will be adjusted according to the minimum threshold rules.
strings.A 10 mm cap against a 3 mm reference giv: A 10 mm cap against a 3 mm reference gives 333 percent. Raising the cap to 12 mm gives 400.
A 10 mm cap against a 3 mm reference gives a maximum suggestion of 333 percent — the ceiling you see repeated across a dry course.
strings.A bulk adjust error means some values ma: A bulk adjust error means some values may already have been written. Check the column before retrying rather than applying twice.
strings.A chevron beside the station name means: A chevron beside the station name means the station has more than one sprinkler paired to it. Without the chevron, the row is the whole story.
strings.A child whose scan is older shows a mode: A child whose scan is older shows a modelled value in grey italics, and the parent average is then part measurement and part model. The parent row is marked the same way so you are not misled.
strings.A clean run confirms that every selected: A clean run confirms that every selected change reached Lynx and verified. Back on the dashboard the pending count is zero and the pushed-today counter has grown by what you sent.
strings.A current scan: black text, today’s date: A current scan: black text, today’s date.
strings.A dash instead of a number: A dash instead of a number
strings.A dash means there is nothing to show: n: A dash means there is nothing to show: no current scan and no modelled value either. It is not zero, and it is not an error in the calculation — the station has no data to calculate from.
strings.A disabled station is excluded from adju: A disabled station is excluded from adjustment entirely; it is not sent a zero, it is simply not sent.
strings.A disabled station: the switch on its ro: A disabled station: the switch on its row is grey.
strings.A failed request says so straight away r: A failed request says so straight away rather than silently doing nothing. If it keeps failing, the diagnostics dialog reports whether the organisation has TurfRad access and whether it has scan data at all — a course-wide problem is almost always there rather than in your settings.
strings.A greyed, italic average means the value: A greyed, italic average means the value came from the model rather than a scan taken that day. The calculation still runs, but it is running on an estimate.
strings.A greyed, italic Avg. VWC with a calcula: A greyed, italic Avg. VWC with a calculator icon means the value was estimated from the model rather than measured by a scan that day.
A modelled value: grey and italic.
strings.A modelled value: grey, italic, and date: A modelled value: grey, italic, and dated two days ago.
strings.A profile changes targets, and targets c: A profile changes targets, and targets change deficits. Scan the Suggested column for stations that jumped to the cap — those are the ones where the new target is a long way from where the station actually is.
strings.A profile is a snapshot, so the work hap: A profile is a snapshot, so the work happens in the table before you save anything. Get the course reading the way you want it, hole by hole, and only then capture it.
A profile per season and per event.
strings.A profile stores one Target VWC per stat: A profile stores one Target VWC per station and nothing else — no percent adjustments, no enable states.
A profile stores one Target VWC per station. It does not store percent adjustments or enable states.
strings.A profile switch queues a large push. Re: A profile switch queues a large push. Review it as one.
strings.A push is four phases, not one. Knowing: A push is four phases, not one. Knowing them tells you whether a slow run is working or stuck.
strings.A queued request confirms immediately; t: A queued request confirms immediately; the data arrives later.
strings.A run of identical suggestions is the si: A run of identical suggestions is the signature of the Max Amount cap.
strings.A run of identical values is the cap, no: A run of identical values is the cap, not a fault.
strings.A scan date older than today means the r: A scan date older than today means the reading is stale. Spatial Adjust falls back to the modelled value, shown in grey italics with a calculator icon. If the whole course is stale, TurfRad has not delivered new scans yet. Use Request latest scan data in the toolbar to queue a retrieval — it takes several minutes and notifies you when it lands, then Reload Data on the banner brings it in.
strings.A short list stays readable a year later: A short list stays readable a year later.
strings.A small set of profiles, one per conditi: A small set of profiles, one per condition, is easier to run a season with than a long list of dated snapshots.
strings.A stale course is not something you have: A stale course is not something you have to wait out. Request a new TurfRad scan, and reload when it lands.
strings.A station at target with a wide spread b: A station at target with a wide spread between heads is a coverage problem, not an irrigation-amount problem.
strings.A station is caught if its suggestion is: A station is caught if its suggestion is above the Over value OR below the Under value. With 200 and 10 set you get everything over 200 percent and everything under 10 percent — and nothing in between. It is an outlier finder. Reading it as “between 10 and 200” gives you exactly the stations it is not showing you.
strings.A station with no current scan and no mo: A station with no current scan and no model estimate shows a dash rather than a number.
strings.A station with the Enable switch off is: A station with the Enable switch off is excluded from adjustment entirely. Disabling an area or hole cascades down, so a station can be off because something above it was turned off.
strings.A successful run confirms every selected: A successful run confirms every selected change reached Lynx. A failure names the number of stations that could not be updated — check the Lynx connection and push those again rather than the whole set.
strings.A target change recalculates that statio: A target change recalculates that station’s suggestion; it does not push anything.
A threshold of 0 disables the feature.
strings.A threshold of zero turns the whole thin: A threshold of zero turns the whole thing off and the option group is disabled with it. If the push dialog shows no banner, check this first — the setting is site-level and someone else may have cleared it.
strings.A whole-number percentage from 0 to 200: A whole-number percentage from 0 to 200 applied to the day’s ET before it enters the calculation. Below 100 the course is treated as using less water than reference ET suggests; above 100, more.
strings.A zero suggestion is usually correct. Fo: A zero suggestion is usually correct. Four checks, in order, tell you whether it is.
strings.Access is granted per user, and the view: Access is granted per user, and the view is admitted only on desktop and tablet.
strings.After a fortnight of individual target e: After a fortnight of individual target edits, the course no longer matches the profile you applied. The profile is still valid, it is simply out of date.
strings.After a recalculation the dashboard relo: After a recalculation the dashboard reloads with new suggestions.
strings.All selected changes pushed and verified: All selected changes pushed and verified.
strings.All selected changes successfully pushed: All selected changes successfully pushed to Lynx.
strings.All Stations carries the full count. Bes: All Stations carries the full count. Beside it, the Over/Under tab carries the count of stations the filter currently catches. Until you set a filter that count is a dash and the tab does nothing — it is not broken, there is simply nothing to show yet.
strings.All three have the same first check: is: All three have the same first check: is the number a measurement, a model, or nothing at all?
Amend a profile without reapplying it.
strings.Amount fields on the Calculation tab sho: Amount fields on the Calculation tab show the unit you chose.
strings.Apply a bulk adjustment — 2 MIN, difficu: Apply a bulk adjustment — 2 MIN, difficulty 2 of 3
strings.Apply a target profile — 2 MIN, difficul: Apply a target profile — 2 MIN, difficulty 1 of 3
strings.Apply the profile the evening before, re: Apply the profile the evening before, review the suggestions the next morning, then push. Applying and pushing in the same minute leaves no time to sanity-check.
strings.Apply to all writes the new targets and: Apply to all writes the new targets and closes the dialog. The suggested percentages recalculate against the new targets straight away, so the Suggested column will move.
strings.Apply, then review the next morning’s su: Apply, then review the next morning’s suggestions.
strings.Applying a profile changes targets on ev: Applying a profile changes targets on every station, which recalculates every suggestion.
strings.Applying a profile is a course-wide chan: Applying a profile is a course-wide change.
strings.Applying a profile is a course-wide reca: Applying a profile is a course-wide recalculation, so treat it as a planned change rather than a quick switch.
strings.Applying overwrites the Target VWC of ev: Applying overwrites the Target VWC of every station the profile covers. Because that is a recalculation input, the dashboard reloads and the Suggested column changes across the course.
strings.Applying rewrites every target and recal: Applying rewrites every target and recalculates every suggestion. Doing it the evening before leaves you the next morning to read the new suggestions against a fresh scan.
strings.At hole and area level the same two colu: At hole and area level the same two columns show averages rather than readings, and the scan date column shows the most recent scan beneath that row. An italic average means at least one child is modelled.
strings.Available only under the second option:: Available only under the second option: a station whose suggestion is a true zero stays at zero instead of being lifted to the threshold. Without it, a station that needs no water gets a small run anyway.
strings.Available to Push comes first, ticked. P: Available to Push comes first, ticked. Pushed Today follows, unticked, and is there to stop you adjusting the same head twice in a day. That hold releases at midnight where the course is, not 24 hours after the push. Tick a pushed station only when you mean to.
strings.Avg / High / Low moisture are computed a: Avg / High / Low moisture are computed across every station in the selected course, not just the ones visible in the table.
strings.Band boundaries and the variance view ar: Band boundaries and the variance view are saved to your own user preferences, not to the site.
strings.Because a cascade can affect dozens of h: Because a cascade can affect dozens of heads, Spatial Adjust asks first and names the scope: this hole and every station beneath it. Continue applies it; Cancel leaves everything as it was.
strings.Because Option 1 scales the current Lynx: Because Option 1 scales the current Lynx value, a station sitting at 0 percent adjust stays at 0 no matter how dry it is.
strings.Before writing anything, Spatial Adjust: Before writing anything, Spatial Adjust retrieves the current percent adjustments from Lynx so it has something to compare against afterwards. On a large course this is the slowest phase.
strings.Below-threshold behaviour, with the seco: Below-threshold behaviour, with the second option selected.
strings.Bulk Adjust dialog. The count confirms y: Bulk Adjust dialog. The count confirms your selection.
strings.Bulk Adjust edits Target VWC, not the pe: Bulk Adjust edits Target VWC, not the percent adjustment.
strings.By the time you see a failure, Spatial A: By the time you see a failure, Spatial Adjust has already retried the affected stations twice.
strings.Calculation ET under the filter tabs is: Calculation ET under the filter tabs is the figure the calculation used. The weather strip reports current conditions separately, so do not expect the two to agree.
strings.Capture the current targets under a name: Capture the current targets under a name.
strings.Capture the station targets you have tun: Capture the station targets you have tuned, under a name you will recognise next season.
strings.Cascading enable state across areas, hol: Cascading enable state across areas, holes and stations.
strings.Change one station’s target and watch wh: Change one station’s target and watch what it does to the suggestion.
strings.Change one station’s Target VWC and see: Change one station’s Target VWC and see the effect.
strings.Change the Target VWC of many stations a: Change the Target VWC of many stations at once, either by replacing every value or by shifting them all by the same amount.
strings.Changing any of them recalculates every: Changing any of them recalculates every suggestion and reloads the dashboard.
strings.Changing Units of Measure and saving in: Changing Units of Measure and saving in the same visit does not re-convert the amounts already on the Calculation tab — they are saved as though they were already in the new unit, which rescales them by 25.4. After a unit change, save, then reopen Settings and check Max Amount and Lynx Reference Amount before you push anything.

strings.Diagnostics: Lynx interconnect, ping, in: Diagnostics: Lynx interconnect, ping, installation ID.
strings.Diagnostics: TurfRad access, scan data,: Diagnostics: TurfRad access, scan data, last scan date.

strings.Dragging a handle changes the boundary a: Dragging a handle changes the boundary and saves it to your preferences.
strings.Each child row is named for its parent a: Each child row is named for its parent and numbered, and carries its own scan date and its own measured moisture. Nothing else is editable at sprinkler level — the target and the adjustment belong to the station.
strings.Each profile shows when it was last appl: Each profile shows when it was last applied and how many stations it covers. The active profile is the one whose targets are currently loaded; changing an individual station target after applying leaves the profile intact but no longer exactly matched.
strings.Each station’s Avg. VWC comes from a Tur: Each station’s Avg. VWC comes from a TurfRad moisture scan — the mean volumetric water content measured across the station, with the date it was captured beside the station name.
strings.Edit the target when the station should: Edit the target when the station should always be wetter or drier. Edit % Adj. when today is unusual.
strings.Editing % Adj. queues the station; the i: Editing % Adj. queues the station; the icon beside the field marks it as pending.

strings.Every station is a pin coloured by its l: Every station is a pin coloured by its latest measured VWC against the four moisture bands in the legend. Drag the handles on the colour bar to move the band boundaries — the map recolours immediately and the change is saved to your user preferences.
strings.Every station is a pin placed at its rea: Every station is a pin placed at its real coordinates and filled with the colour of the moisture band its latest reading falls into. Four bands by default: 0–5, 6–19, 20–30, and above 30 percent.
strings.Every station row carries the date its r: Every station row carries the date its reading was captured. One stale row is a station; a column of stale dates is the whole course, and that is a supply problem rather than a settings problem.
strings.Every station you edited shows the pendi: Every station you edited shows the pending push icon beside the % Adj. field.
strings.Every suggestion in this column came fro: Every suggestion in this column came from that chain.
strings.Everything in the dialog is still revers: Everything in the dialog is still reversible. Nothing is written until you use the footer button.
strings.Exclude Zeros is disabled until Under is: Exclude Zeros is disabled until Under is on.
strings.Exclude Zeros is enabled only for the se: Exclude Zeros is enabled only for the second option.
strings.Exclude Zeros is greyed out until Under: Exclude Zeros is greyed out until Under is enabled, because a zero is below any under-threshold and the option means nothing without one. Tick it and genuine zeros drop out of the filter, leaving the stations that asked for a little rather than the ones that asked for nothing. Your thresholds are saved to your own user preferences, not to the site.
strings.Failed stations are re-pushed automatica: Failed stations are re-pushed automatically, up to two further attempts. Pushing again by hand immediately afterwards is a fourth attempt at the same connection, which rarely behaves differently.

strings.The button beside the legend switches th: The button beside the legend switches the pins from absolute moisture to variance — how far each station sits from its target rather than its raw reading.
strings.The button beside the legend toggles bet: The button beside the legend toggles between VWC and variance. Variance colours each pin by how far it sits from its own target instead of by its raw reading, which is the view you want when targets differ across the course.
strings.The button carries the number of station: The button carries the number of stations with an unpushed edit. It is disabled when nothing is queued, so a greyed-out button means there is nothing to review.
strings.The button reads the number of stations: The button reads the number of stations with an unpushed edit. Beside it the green counter shows how many have already gone out today. If Push Changes is greyed out there is nothing queued.
strings.The button stays disabled until at least: The button stays disabled until at least one row checkbox is ticked.
strings.The calculation starts from the differen: The calculation starts from the difference between measured moisture and the station target, converts that into an amount of water, adds today’s ET, and expresses the result as a percentage of the Lynx reference amount. A station well under target asks for more water; one over target asks for less.

strings.The circular-arrow button in the toolbar: The circular-arrow button in the toolbar’s right-hand group is Request latest scan data. It asks TurfRad for a new scan; it does not reload the dashboard, and it does not change a single calculation setting.

strings.When the scan is not current, Spatial Ad: When the scan is not current, Spatial Adjust falls back to a modelled value carried forward from the last scan and the weather since. It is shown in grey italics so you can tell it apart at a glance.
